Emergency Preparedness — City of Fremont

The City of Fremont's Office of Emergency Services (OES), a division of the Fire Department, plans for natural disasters and other highly complex emergencies. Fremont publishes preparedness guidance for: earthquakes, wildfire, storms and flooding, tsunamis, hot weather and cooling centers, power outages (PG&E safety tips and alerts), and evacuation.

Residents are urged to: make a plan, gather supplies, get notified (emergency alerts signup), and check the Natural Hazards Map.

When a major incident occurs, the City's Emergency Operations Center (EOC) may be activated. The EOC coordinates emergency operations, information management, and resources including mutual aid and State and Federal assistance, staffed by representatives of all City agencies and liaisons from other public agencies and non-governmental partners, coordinating closely with Alameda County emergency management. OES manages the EOC under the executive direction of the City Manager, who is Director of Emergency Services.

Phases of emergency management: Preparedness (planning, training, exercises before an incident); Response (immediate actions during an incident to safeguard life safety, property, and the environment); Recovery (restoring services and rebuilding after an incident); Mitigation (actions to reduce long-term risk from disasters).

The Disaster Council develops and recommends emergency plans, policies, and agreements for City Council adoption, per Fremont Municipal Code Article I, Section 2.20. The City Council adopted the Emergency Operations Plan in February 2020 and the 2024 Tri-City Multi-jurisdictional Local Hazard Mitigation Plan in November 2024.

Volunteer opportunities include: Adopt-a-Drain, American Red Cross Sheltering and Disaster Health Services, the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Program, the Fire Department Rehabilitation Unit, the Medical Reserve Corps, the Tri-City Animal Shelter, and Volunteers in Police Services (VIPS).

Earthquake Preparedness — City of Fremont

What to do in an earthquake: if indoors, Drop, Cover, and Hold On — protect yourself from falling and shifting objects. If in bed, stay there and cover your head and neck with a pillow. If driving, pull over, stop, set the parking brake, and stay clear of overpasses, bridges, and overhead hazards such as power lines. Safety guidance is published in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, Hindi, Spanish, and Vietnamese.

How to prepare: practice with the Great ShakeOut (October 15, 2026 at 10:15 am). Follow the 7 Steps to Earthquake Safety. Financial help exists for retrofits: up to $3,000 for home foundation seismic retrofits for qualifying homes built before 1980 with raised foundations or crawlspaces, and up to $13,000 for soft-story home seismic retrofits for qualifying homes built before 2000 with living space above the garage — get notified when registration opens. Whether you rent or own, consider earthquake insurance. Get early earthquake warnings on your phone with the earthquake warning app. Secure your water heater now to prevent gas and water leaks and fires.

Wildfire Preparedness — City of Fremont

Maintaining proper clearance around your home dramatically increases the chance of your house surviving a wildfire. Keep your property lean and green (defensible space) to protect your family and home. Defensible Space requirements apply to Fremont property owners within the City's Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (VHFHSZ), as designated by local ordinance — enter your address in the City's map to see if your home is in the zone.

Prepare for wildfire: make a Wildfire Action Plan, know evacuation routes, sign up for emergency alerts, and follow equipment and vehicle fire safety guidance.
